one_line: Architect-priest of the Charaideo maidams and the Ahom king who reformed royal burials in Upper Assam.

appearance.age_look: early 30s for Chang-Rung Phukan, late 30s for Rudra Singha; both lean, athletic builds
appearance.face: Chang-Rung Phukan: oval face, light brown complexion with a warm undertone, straight nose, sharp cheekbones, single-lid almond eyes with a focused gaze and a calm, analytical default expression; Rudra Singha: slightly broader face, similar light brown complexion, strong jawline, thicker brows, intense but composed eyes with a slight upward tilt and a resolute, protective default expression.
appearance.hair: Chang-Rung Phukan: straight black hair gathered into a neat topknot at the back of the crown, wrapped with a narrow white cloth band; Rudra Singha: straight black hair tied into a higher, slightly fuller topknot, secured with a deep-red cloth band and a small plain gold hair pin.
appearance.costume: Chang-Rung Phukan wears a long off-white muga-silk tunic reaching mid-thigh, with a subtle woven sheen and side slits over a mustard-gold cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and knotted at the front, pleats falling neatly to the ankles; over this, he drapes a pale cream and light-green striped gamocha-style shawl over the left shoulder and across the chest, the ends hanging at hip level, the edges bearing a narrow red woven border; his waist is cinched with a simple braided jute-coloured cloth belt; he is barefoot or in simple brown leather sandals; jewellery is modest—a thin gold necklace, small plain gold ear-studs and a single copper bangle on the right wrist; Rudra Singha wears a rich deep-red silk jama-style long coat, fitted at the torso and flaring gently from the waist to just below the knees, fastened diagonally across the chest with small cloth buttons, the coat hem and cuffs trimmed with a narrow golden-yellow border; beneath, he has a cream-coloured cotton churidar-style lower garment gathered at the ankles; around his waist a broad golden-yellow cloth sash is wrapped, knotted slightly off-centre with the ends hanging to mid-thigh; he drapes a white muga-silk shawl with thin red borders over both shoulders like a royal angavastra; his footwear is brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; jewellery includes a medium-width gold armlet on the right arm, a simple gold ring on his left hand, and small round gold earrings; both costumes remain modest and fully cover torso and legs in era-appropriate Assamese-Ahom style textiles.
appearance.signature: Chang-Rung Phukan holds a long bamboo measuring staff marked with carved notches in one hand and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord in the other, while Rudra Singha rests his hand on the hilt of a sheathed straight single-edged Ahom sword with a simple brown wooden scabbard and plain brass fittings hanging from his sash.

ref_desc: Chang-Rung Phukan and Rudra Singha appear together: light-brown complexions, sharp almond-eyed faces, black hair in cloth-wrapped topknots, the architect-priest in off-white tunic, mustard-gold dhoti and green-striped shawl with bamboo measuring staff and manuscript, and the king in deep-red silk coat, cream lowers, golden-yellow sash and white muga shawl resting his hand on a sheathed straight Ahom sword, all in Assamese-Ahom colours of off-white, mustard-gold, deep red and golden yellow.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two fixed characters from early modern Ahom Assam, standing side by side against a plain background so their designs are clear: first, Chang-Rung Phukan, with a light-brown complexion, lean build, oval face, sharp single-lid almond eyes and calm analytical expression, straight black hair pulled into a neat topknot wrapped with a narrow white cloth band; he wears a long off-white muga-silk tunic to mid-thigh with subtle sheen and side slits, a mustard-gold cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and knotted at the front with clean pleats to the ankles, a pale cream and light-green striped gamocha-style shawl with a narrow red border draped from the left shoulder across the chest, a simple jute-coloured cloth belt at the waist, is barefoot or in simple brown leather sandals, and has modest jewellery: thin gold necklace, small gold ear-studs and a single copper bangle on the right wrist; he holds a long bamboo measuring staff marked with carved notches in one hand and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord in the other. Beside him, draw Rudra Singha with a slightly broader but still lean build, light-brown complexion, strong jaw, thick brows, intense yet composed eyes and a resolute expression, straight black hair tied in a fuller topknot secured with a deep-red cloth band and a small plain gold pin; he wears a deep-red silk jama-style long coat fitted through the torso and flaring below the waist to just past the knees, fastened diagonally across the chest with small cloth buttons, the hem and cuffs edged with a narrow golden-yellow border, over cream cotton churidar-style lower garments gathered at the ankles, a broad golden-yellow cloth sash around his waist with the ends hanging to mid-thigh, and a white muga-silk shawl with thin red borders draped over both shoulders like a royal angavastra; he wears brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes and simple royal jewellery: a gold armlet on the right arm, a plain gold ring on the left hand and small round gold earrings; his right hand rests on the hilt of a sheathed straight single-edged Ahom sword with a brown wooden scabbard and plain brass fittings hanging from his sash; keep both characters fully clothed, dignified, with clear Assamese-Ahom textile textures and the shared colour palette of off-white, mustard-gold, deep red, golden yellow and light green, shown from head to toe for consistent redraws.
